unfold.unfolded:
Let $G$, $T$, $P$, $\lambda$, $S$, $t\in T$ and $r\geq 1$ be as in the paper, with $G$ a connected reductive group, $T$ a maximal torus, $P$ a parabolic subgroup and $\lambda$ a weight. Let $Y_S$ be the set of $v\in W^P$ with $B^S\cdot vP/P=vP/P$, which index the connected components $X_P^t(v)$ of $X_P^S$. For $v\in Y_S$ let $d_v$ be the integer attached to $v$, and let $D_v^t(n,\lambda)$ be the function
\[
D_v^t(n,\lambda)=\sum_{k\geq 0}\int_{X_P^t(v)}\frac{c_1\bigl(\mathcal{L}(\lambda)|_{X_P^t(v)}\bigr)^k\,\frac{n^k}{k!}\,e^{-nv\lambda}(t)\cdot\mathrm{td}(X_P^t(v))}{\prod_{\alpha\in (vR_P^+)\setminus R((G^t)^o)}\bigl[1-e^\alpha(t)\,e^{-c_1(\overline{\mathcal{L}}(\alpha)|_{X_P^t(v)})}\bigr]}
\]
whose sum over $v\in Y_S$ gives $\mathrm{ch}(t^{-1},V(n\lambda))$ for every integer $n\geq 0$. Fix $p$ with $0\leq p<r$. Then the restriction of $\chi^t_\lambda$ to $\{n\equiv p\ (\mathrm{mod}\ r)\}$ is a polynomial function in $n$ of degree at most $\max_{v\in Y_S}\{d_v\}$. Moreover, the coefficient of $n^{d_v}$ in $D_v^t(n,\lambda)$ restricted to $\{n\equiv p\ (\mathrm{mod}\ r)\}$ equals
\[
\frac{1}{d_v!}\int_{X_P^t(v)} c_1\bigl(\mathcal{L}(\lambda)|_{X_P^t(v)}\bigr)^{d_v}\,\frac{e^{-pv\lambda}(t)}{\prod_{\alpha\in (vR_P^+)\setminus R((G^t)^o)}(1-e^\alpha(t))}.
\]
